title: Inequalities
goal: Use IN 1–IN 3, solve linear inequalities, and write the answer as an interval.
generalHint: Multiply or divide by a negative number: the sign of the inequality turns around. Look at the mirror screen.

screens.label: RECALL
screens.title: A negative power

mistakes.reply: A negative exponent does not make a negative number. Find 1/16^(1/2).
The minus sign in the exponent means one over. What is 1/√16?

hints: A negative exponent means one over the power.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: Multiply by −2
screens.prompt: You know that $1 < 3$. Multiply the two sides by $-2$. Is $-2 < -6$ true? Make a guess.

options.label: True
options.reply: Look at the line: −6 is to the left of −2. Which number is smaller?

feedback.correctWhy: On the line, −6 is left of −2. So −2 > −6. The sign turns around.

hints: Put −2 and −6 on the number line.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: The mirror changes the order
screens.prompt: Multiplying by $-1$ mirrors points across 0. On the line, 1 is left of 3. After the mirror, where are $-1$ and $-3$?

options.reply: The mirror swaps left and right. Is −1 left of −3?

feedback.correctWhy: The mirror turns the order around. 1 < 3 becomes −1 > −3.

screens.caption: Choose an answer, then check.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Greater than
screens.prompt: $a > b$ means $a - b > 0$. These three rules follow. IN 1: if $a > b$ and $b > c$, then $a > c$. IN 2: multiply by $c > 0$. IN 3: multiply by $c < 0$ and the sign turns around.

note.label: WORDS MATTER
note.text: Greater than means: the difference is positive.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: IN 1
screens.prompt: Prove IN 1: if $a > b$ and $b > c$, then $a > c$. Use the meaning of $>$. Then use POS 1.

wrongReasonReplies.def-gt: This step uses the meaning: a > b means a − b > 0. Did a line change a comparison into a difference?
wrongReasonReplies.POS1: POS 1 says that the sum of positive numbers is positive. Which line adds two positive numbers?
wrongReasonReplies.simplify: This step cancels terms. Which line has b and −b together?
wrongReasonReplies.def-gt-back: This step reads the meaning backwards: a positive difference gives a comparison.
wrongReasonReplies.POS2: POS 2 gives three cases for one number. Is there a case split here?
wrongReasonReplies.IN2: IN 2 multiplies by a positive number. Is there a multiplication in this step?

feedback.correctWhy: The sum of two positive numbers is positive. Here a − b and b − c are positive, so a − c is positive.

screens.caption: Tap a reason to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Intervals
screens.prompt: A filled dot includes an end. An empty dot excludes it. An infinite interval, for example $x > 7$, has one end only. Draw $-2 < x \le 5$. Drag the orange ends and tap the end buttons.

answer.correctWhy: The end −2 is empty because x is greater than −2. The end 5 is filled because x can equal 5.

mistakes.reply: The end at −2 is empty, because x > −2. Which end is filled?
The end at 5 is filled, because x ≤ 5 includes 5.
The end at −2 is empty and the end at 5 is filled. You have them the other way.
Move the left end to −2. The interval starts at −2.

hints: Empty dot: the end is not included.
Filled dot: the end is included.
screens.caption: Draw the interval, then check.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 3
screens.title: Solve −2x + 1 < 5
screens.prompt: Solve the inequality. Type the answer, for example $x > 3$ or $(3, \infty)$.

answer.correctWhy: −2x < 4. Divide by −2 and turn the sign around: x > −2.

mistakes.reply: You divided by −2. Look at the mirror screen. What happens to the inequality sign?

hints: Divide by $-2$. Turn the sign around.

steps.text: Divide by −2. The sign turns around (IN 3).

answer.correctWhy: −2x < 8. Divide by −2 and turn the sign around: x > −4.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 3
screens.title: Solve 3x + 2 < 1
screens.prompt: Solve the inequality. Type the answer.

answer.correctWhy: 3x < −1. Divide by 3. The sign stays: x < −1/3.

mistakes.reply: Divide by 3, a positive number. Does the sign turn around?
3x < 1 − 2 = −1. Check the sign of the right side.

hints: Divide by 3. It is a positive number.

answer.correctWhy: 4x < −1. Divide by 4. The sign stays: x < −1/4.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 3 OF 3
screens.title: Cases
screens.prompt: Solve $\dfrac{2x-1}{x+2} < 1$. Examine the cases $x > -2$ and $x < -2$ separately.

answer.correctWhy: If x > −2: 2x − 1 < x + 2, so x < 3. If x < −2: 2x − 1 > x + 2, so x > 3. That is impossible.

mistakes.reply: The sign of x + 2 is not known. Examine x + 2 > 0 and x + 2 < 0 separately.

hints: If $x + 2 > 0$, multiply by $x + 2$. The sign stays.

steps.text: Multiply by $x + 2 < 0$. The sign turns around. No $x$ fits.
Only the first case gives numbers.

answer.correctWhy: If x > −1: 3x + 1 < 2x + 2, so x < 1. If x < −1: 3x + 1 > 2x + 2, so x > 1. That is impossible.

trap.question: True or false: if you multiply the two sides of an inequality by a number, the inequality stays the same.

feedback.correctWhy: If you multiply by a negative number, the sign turns around. For 1 < 3 and −2: −2 > −6.
